title: The new back page
venue: the coast community-college paper, Newport · the laundromat digest
source: lore/drift_wood/_THE_COMPLETE_RUN.md (1999–2000 · deepening xix · the daily filled)
logline: The Timberline's first issue of the year, in the laundromat's rack beside the digest. The back page has a strip now. Someone else's. Wood reads it standing up. It's bad. He's relieved. Then he isn't. He puts it back behind the digest.

panels.composition: The laundromat rack: the digest, and beside it a school paper, folded. WOOD taking the paper. BARNABY.

image.prompt: a young man taking a folded school newspaper from a wire rack beside small booklets in a laundromat, black and white, no words

panels.composition: The back page: a four-panel strip in someone else's line — round, careful, a joke about a locker. Drawn as blocks with the shapes of a strip.

image.prompt: close on a school newspaper's back page with a four-panel comic strip in a round careful line, its content rendered as blocks, black and white, no words
image.notes: The new back page: someone else's. Reserved who.

panels.composition: Wood's face, reading. Relief. Then the other thing.

image.prompt: a young man's face reading a newspaper: relief, then something worse, black and white, no words

panels.composition: Wood putting the paper back. Behind the digest. The LAUNDRY owner watching. Not saying anything. She saw both faces.

image.prompt: a young man placing a folded school newspaper behind small booklets in a wire rack while a laundromat owner watches, black and white, no words

art.line: brush-pen, committed; black and white; xerox

notes: The back page has someone else's strip. Both faces. She saw them.
